name: Array Intrinsics: MATMUL, SUM, MAXVAL, TRANSPOSE
description: Intrinsic lowering paths: MATMUL → _FortranAMatmul runtime call; SUM/MAXVAL → inline loop or _FortranASum; TRANSPOSE → hlfir.elemental with swapped indices
source:
subroutine matrix_ops(c, a, b, n, m, k)
  implicit none
  integer, intent(in)  :: n, m, k
  real,    intent(in)  :: a(n,m), b(m,k)
  real,    intent(out) :: c(n,k)

  c = MATMUL(a, b)

end subroutine matrix_ops

semantics.content:
Symbol table: matrix_ops
  c: rank=2 REAL(4) intent=IntentOut  shape=(1:n,1:k)
  a: rank=2 REAL(4) intent=IntentIn   shape=(1:n,1:m)
  b: rank=2 REAL(4) intent=IntentIn   shape=(1:m,1:k)
  n, m, k: rank=0 INTEGER(4) intent=IntentIn

MATMUL analysis:
  Classification: TRANSFORMATIONAL intrinsic (not elemental)
  Arguments: a(n,m), b(m,k) — inner dimensions must match: a%dim(2) == b%dim(1)
  Result: c(n,k) — outer dimensions
  Conformance check: m == m ✓
  Lowering strategy:
    1. Allocate temporary !hlfir.expr<?x?xf32> of shape (n,k)
    2. Call @_FortranAMatmul(result_desc, a_desc, b_desc) — runtime does the work
    3. Copy temp into c using hlfir.assign
    4. Destroy temp (hlfir.destroy)
  Why runtime? Matrix multiply is not elemental — it has a reduction dimension
    that cannot be expressed as a simple hlfir.elemental body.

llvm_ir.content:
; ModuleID = '08_intrinsics.f90'
; Runtime ABI for transformational intrinsics
declare void @_FortranAMatmul(ptr, ptr, ptr, ptr, i32, i32)
declare void @_FortranAAssign(ptr, ptr, ptr, i32, i32)

define void @_QPmatrix_ops(
    ptr nocapture %0,   ; c(n,k)
    ptr nocapture readonly %1,  ; a(n,m)
    ptr nocapture readonly %2,  ; b(m,k)
    ptr nocapture readonly %3,  ; n
    ptr nocapture readonly %4,  ; m
    ptr nocapture readonly %5   ; k
) #0 !dbg !5 {
entry:
  %n = load i32, ptr %3, align 4
  %m = load i32, ptr %4, align 4
  %k = load i32, ptr %5, align 4
  %n_64 = sext i32 %n to i64
  %m_64 = sext i32 %m to i64
  %k_64 = sext i32 %k to i64

  ; Build Fortran array descriptor for a (on stack)
  %a_desc = alloca %Descriptor, align 8
  ; Populate: base_addr=a, rank=2, extent0=n, extent1=m, stride0=1, stride1=n
  store ptr %1, ptr %a_desc, align 8
  ; ... (descriptor field population omitted for brevity)

  ; Build descriptor for b
  %b_desc = alloca %Descriptor, align 8
  store ptr %2, ptr %b_desc, align 8

  ; Allocate result descriptor on stack; _FortranAMatmul will heap-allocate the data
  %result_desc = alloca %Descriptor, align 8
  ; Zero-initialize so _FortranAMatmul knows to allocate
  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr %result_desc, i8 0, i64 72, i1 false)

  ; Call MATMUL runtime — does the actual matrix multiplication
  ; ABI: (result_desc, a_desc, b_desc, src_file, src_line)
  call void @_FortranAMatmul(ptr %result_desc, ptr %a_desc, ptr %b_desc,
                              ptr @.str_file, i32 8, i32 3), !dbg !11

  ; Build descriptor for c (output)
  %c_desc = alloca %Descriptor, align 8
  store ptr %0, ptr %c_desc, align 8
  ; ... extent/stride population

  ; Copy result into c
  call void @_FortranAAssign(ptr %c_desc, ptr %result_desc,
                              ptr @.str_file, i32 8, i32 3), !dbg !11

  ; Free the heap-allocated result buffer
  %data_ptr = load ptr, ptr %result_desc, align 8
  call void @_FortranAFreeMemory(ptr %data_ptr)

  ret void, !dbg !12
}

; CRITICAL INSIGHT: MATMUL generates 3 stack-allocated Fortran descriptors
; and delegates all computation to _FortranAMatmul. The descriptor ABI carries
; rank, extents, strides, base_addr — allowing the runtime to handle arbitrary
; column-major arrays without knowing sizes at compile time.

!5  = distinct !DISubprogram(name: "matrix_ops", line: 4)
!11 = !DILocation(line: 11, column: 3, scope: !5)
!12 = !DILocation(line: 13, column: 1, scope: !5)

correlations.lowering_notes: MATMUL is a transformational (not elemental) intrinsic — its result depends on reductions across the inner dimension. Flang cannot express it as hlfir.elemental. Instead, HLFIR introduces hlfir.matmul as a distinct op that lowers to embox (building Fortran array descriptors on the stack) + _FortranAMatmul runtime call + _FortranAAssign to copy the heap-allocated result into c + _FortranAFreeMemory. Three stack-allocated descriptors encode rank, extents, strides, and base pointers for the Fortran runtime ABI.

lowering_patterns.name: Transformational Intrinsic → Runtime ABI
lowering_patterns.description: MATMUL, SUM, MAXVAL (and other transformational intrinsics) lower to calls into the Fortran runtime library via descriptor ABI — stack-allocated structs encoding rank, extents, strides, and base_addr

lowering_patterns.name: hlfir.matmul op
lowering_patterns.description: HLFIR introduces intrinsic-specific ops (hlfir.matmul, hlfir.sum, hlfir.maxval) that preserve the high-level semantics for optimization passes before lowering to FIR runtime calls

lowering_patterns.name: Heap Temporary Lifecycle
lowering_patterns.description: Non-elemental intrinsic results (type !hlfir.expr) represent heap-allocated temporaries; hlfir.destroy emits _FortranAFreeMemory to release them after use
